title: Case: City-centre framing workshop has a boxed order waiting for collection since Monday
context: Yardley Frames ships regularly with Thistlecombe Arc Logistics and books collections in the Business portal. DL-3630, one boxed frame order, has been waiting for collection at the workshop. The shipper account is verified.
initial_request: FOUR DAYS, NO COLLECTION. Same as the last time and the time before that. I complain, it gets rebooked for tomorrow, nobody comes, the ticket closes itself, a new ticket appears, repeat. We are on Tanner's Row, right in the middle of the city, your vans go past the workshop window every single day. I'm here eight till six with the door propped open. There's another one booked for today, COL-5156, and I expect it will go the same way. I don't honestly know what else to ask for any more. Just please don't write back to tell me it's been rebooked.

acceptable_actions.summary: Asks Collections control to review the stop for DL-3630 against the driver route sheets after four failed collections, listing the dates and the closed ticket numbers.

must: Asks Collections control, on the Depot work queue, to review the collection stop for DL-3630 against the driver route sheets and say why the collections are failing.
Lists the four failed collections on 7, 8, 9 and 9 September with the closed tickets COL-1686, COL-3405, COL-7403 and COL-1299, and the open ticket COL-5156 for 10 September.
States the shipper's account that the workshop on Tanner's Row is staffed 08:00 to 18:00 with the door open and the parcel waiting by the door.

Tells Collections control that this shipper has had the same rebook-and-close cycle before and that each rebooking wipes the history, so the review is prioritised and not answered with another rebooking.
must_not: Rebooks the collection for another day, or asks Umberlea to rebook it.
Tells the shipper that today's collection under COL-5156 will happen, or that the collection has been rebooked.
Brings DL-5453, its proof of delivery, the August invoice or the promotional offer into the message.
States as fact that drivers are skipping the stop, or suggests the shipper was not there to hand the parcel over.
Sends the request to Umberlea again, who have said they can only rebook and cannot see the earlier attempts.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: DL-3630, Yardley Frames, Tanner's Row: stop review requested after four failed collections. Umberlea have told me that three or more failures on one shipment come to you and that you hold the driver route sheets. Failed collections, all booked 13:00 to 17:00: 6 September (COL-1686, closed), 7 September (COL-3405, closed), 8 September (COL-7403, closed), 9 September (COL-1299, closed). A fifth is booked for today, 10 September, under COL-5156. Each rebooking closed the ticket before it, so Umberlea cannot see why any attempt failed and no reason has been given to the shipper. The shipper, Gideon Yardley, says the workshop is staffed 08:00 to 18:00 with the door open, the parcel is boxed and waiting by the door, and Thistlecombe Arc vans pass the window daily. I have not verified why the stop is being missed. Please check the route sheets for those four dates, tell me what the drivers recorded at this stop, and say what will be different for today's collection. She tells me this is not the first time she has been through this cycle and she has all but given up asking, so please do not answer this with another rebooking.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3108: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
